# Aurion Creative: December Execution Blueprint

&#32;Nov 14, 2026 · @Thato

Every decision in this blueprint is already made, so December is execution only: tick the boxes in order, paste the scripts from the Scripts tab, and run the prompts from the Claude Code prompts tab.

## 1. Business model: an engineering-led studio, with products as proof

Aurion Creative is an engineering-led software studio: it designs, builds and runs automation and custom platforms for technical businesses, and its own products prove that it can.

**The position. Use these words on every surface.**

- **What Aurion is:** an engineering-led software studio. Engineering and technology in one firm, founded by a mechanical engineer.
- **Who it serves:** businesses whose work is technical and document-heavy. Engineering and construction offices first, then compliance and development teams, then any operation where an error in a document costs money.
- **How it works, the Aurion method:** Specify, Build, Test on real work, Commission, Monitor. These are engineering habits, and most software firms skip the third and fourth.
- **The line:** "Engineering meets software."
- **Descriptor under the logo:** Engineering-led software studio.

**What the products are for.** The Command Centre and BeeLevel are not what Aurion is. They are two systems Aurion designed, built and runs, shown as products and as evidence of capability. Each also opens a door, because a specific tool earns a reply where a studio pitch does not. Outreach therefore leads with the product that fits the audience, and the audit decides whether the client needs that product or a custom build.

**Offers and prices**

| Offer | What it is | Price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workflow Audit | The paid first step for every client. A 60-minute call and a two-page plan showing hours saved. The fee is credited against any build | R 3 500 |
| Custom build | A system designed around one client's process and delivered with the Aurion method. Always a fixed price, quoted in three options | From R 45 000 setup, then from R 4 500 a month to run and maintain |
| Command Centre | Aurion's product for engineering and construction offices: BOQs, tenders and site reports. Its own line is "It asks before it assumes" | One module R 38 000 and R 4 900 a month. Two modules R 62 000 and R 7 900. All three R 85 000 and R 10 900 |
| BeeLevel | Aurion's product for enterprise and supplier development teams, at beelevel.co.za. It keeps records and evidence ready for verification and never calculates B-BBEE points or levels | Founding pilot R 7 500 a month for three months, then from R 15 000 a month, indicative |
| Enquiry Desk | Website section and WhatsApp assistant that qualifies enquiries and books calls | R 15 000, then R 1 900 a month |

Terms for custom builds and the Command Centre: 12-month term, 50% deposit to start, the second 50% only once the system passes its test on the client's own files, monthly fee by debit order on the 1st, and a delivery date fixed in the proposal. The Command Centre onboards inside 30 working days.

**Founding Office offer.** The first three clients that sign a custom build or a Command Centre package by 31 Mar 2027 get 40% off setup, so one Command Centre module costs R 22 800. In return they give measured before-and-after numbers, a written testimonial, logo use and two reference calls. After three it closes.

**Guarantee.** If the Workflow Audit does not find at least 10 hours a month to save, it is free.

**Target.** Six retained clients across custom builds and products, at an average of R 5 900 a month, is R 35 400 recurring by December 2027. The cap is eight clients while you have a day job.

**Ten rules that keep it premium**

1. Never quote an hourly rate.
2. Never publish a price below R 15 000, except the audit.
3. No free builds and no trial projects. The audit is the trial.
4. Every proposal shows three options with the middle one recommended.
5. Every claim on the site has a name or a number behind it.
6. Two onboardings a month at most, and say so publicly.
7. Decline generic websites and chatbots that have no process problem behind them. Existing clients stay on their care plans.
8. Reply within one working evening, every time.
9. Every document you send is branded, dated and versioned.
10. Raise prices 10% after every third client.

**Delete in December:** the "from R3,500" pricing, the instant quote calculator, the spa, apparel and magazine portfolio pieces, any statistic you cannot prove, and any testimonial without written consent.

## 3. Marketing plan, part 1: rules, targets and channels 1 to 5

Twelve channels run in parallel so no single one can sink the month, and each has a number you control. Every script named below (W1, L1, E1 and so on) is in the Scripts tab, ready to paste.

**Which product leads where**

| Audience | Lead with | Free first step | What the audit or demo sells |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Engineering and construction offices | The Command Centre | BOQ Checker | The Command Centre, or a custom build |
| ESD managers and implementers | BeeLevel | Five-minute demo and the free plan | A BeeLevel pilot |
| Any technical business that finds you | The studio and its method | Workflow Audit | A custom build |

December's volume goes to the first row, because that audience is the largest and the easiest to reach. Channel 12 covers the second row, and the site, the reels and the talks cover the third.

**Three rules before anything is sent**

1. **Ask permission first.** Under POPIA section 69, the first electronic message to a business that is not your customer must only ask for consent. An opt-out line is not consent and silence is not consent, and this covers companies as well as people ([Information Regulator guidance](https://inforegulator.org.za/popia/), [plain-language summary](https://mjkinc.co.za/popia/electronic-marketing-section-69)). Every first-contact script here is a permission ask. Log each yes and no. Never message a no again. This is not legal advice.
2. **Send by hand.** No tool logs into your LinkedIn account. Software prepares lists and drafts; you press send. Free accounts get about 100 invitations a week and five invitation notes a month ([limits](https://expandi.io/blog/linkedin-connections-limit)), so invitations go out blank.
3. **Respect the builders' break.** Most of the construction sector closes from around 16 Dec until the second week of January ([Leads 2 Business](https://www.l2b.co.za/Construction-News/Most-contractors-in-SA-will-close-for-the-builders?Id=cefdd158-3fea-4e72-a314-a4421a15a9f6&strLength=short)). Outreach to firms runs 1 to 11 Dec and restarts on 12 Jan.

**December targets**

| Channel | What you do in December |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Warm network | 40 messages sent |
| 2. LinkedIn | 105 blank invitations, 35 permission messages |
| 3. Firm email | 60 permission emails |
| 4. Partners | 20 partner emails, 3 calls |
| 5. Reels and posts | 12 reels and 12 posts made and scheduled |
| 6. BOQ Checker | Live by 8 Dec |
| 7. Search | 3 service pages, 4 articles, Google Business Profile |
| 8. Talks | 6 pitches |
| 9. Trade press | 4 pitches |
| 10. Communities | 4 groups joined, 1 post each |
| 11. Past clients | Every past client contacted |
| 12. BeeLevel's audience | 30 blank invitations, 8 permission emails |

The outcome to aim for: five Workflow Audits booked for January and one Founding Office signed by 31 Jan 2027.

**The tracker.** On 1 Dec create a Google Sheet called Aurion Pipeline with these columns: Firm, Type, Town, Website, Contact, Role, LinkedIn URL, Email, Source, First contact date, Channel, Consent, Stage, Next action, Next date, Notes. It moves into Aurion Desk on 15 Dec.

## 4. Marketing plan, part 2: channels 6 to 11

These seven channels keep producing after you start work, because each one is something people find or attend without you chasing them.

### Channel 6: BOQ Checker, the free tool (build 4 to 5 Dec, live by 8 Dec)

A visitor uploads a BOQ spreadsheet and gets a report of arithmetic errors, missing rates and inconsistent units. It proves the product in two minutes and collects consent properly.

- [ ] Run Prompt 2 in Claude Code and deploy it at aurioncreative.com/boq-checker
- [ ] Test it with five real BOQs from your BOQ client, with their permission, and fix what it misses
- [ ] Confirm the form has an unticked consent box reading "Email me the report and occasional notes on BOQ and tender automation". A tick is your POPIA consent, and it starts the nurture sequence

## 6. Sales department

Every lead moves through the same eight stages, and the paid audit is the only door into a build.

**Stages, used in the tracker and in Aurion Desk:** New, Permission given, Checker used, Audit booked, Audit done, Proposal sent, Signed, Not now.

**Set up once (4 and 21 Dec)**

- [ ] In Cal.com, create the event "Workflow Audit, 60 minutes". Slots: Tuesday and Thursday 19:30, Saturday 09:00 and 10:30. Minimum notice 24 hours. Until 11 Dec also open weekdays 10:00 and 14:00
- [ ] Add the five pre-call questions from script S0 to the booking form, including a file upload for one sample BOQ or tender
- [ ] Create a R 3 500 payment link in Paystack or Yoco and put it in the booking confirmation email. The audit is paid before the call
- [ ] Build the proposal template from script S3: three options, the middle one marked Recommended, valid 14 days, deposit link at the bottom

**Every audit, the same way**

- [ ] Open the call by asking permission to record it
- [ ] Ask the ten questions in script S1, in order
- [ ] Within 24 hours, paste the transcript into Claude with prompt S2 to draft the two-page plan. Edit it for 20 minutes
- [ ] Send the plan and the proposal together
- [ ] Follow up on day 2 (any questions), day 6 (offer a 15-minute call) and day 13 (the offer lapses tomorrow). Then mark Not now and set a reminder for 90 days

**Pricing rules**

- No discount beyond the Founding Office offer. If the price is too high, remove a module instead.
- No work starts before the deposit clears.
- Objections are answered from script S4, word for word.

**Custom builds.** When the audit points to a custom build instead of a product, the three options in the proposal are three scopes, essential, recommended and complete, each a fixed price from R 45 000.

## 7. Delivery and product department (18 to 19 Dec)

A client must be able to see the product working on realistic files before they pay, and go live only when its output matches their own.

- [ ] Call the product the Command Centre everywhere a client can see it. Internal names can stay
- [ ] Run Prompt 5 to build a demo office: one fictional practice, three projects, synthetic BOQs, one tender pack and a week of site notes. No client data
- [ ] Seed five open questions in the clarification queue, so the demo shows the product asking before it assumes
- [ ] Record two demos from it: 90 seconds for messages and five minutes for the site
- [ ] Write the client's one-page onboarding plan, 30 working days:

| Week | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Kickoff call. Client sends ten past files and their templates |
| 2 | You configure the module to their templates |
| 3 | It runs on their files beside their manual process |
| 4 | 45-minute recorded training for two users, then go-live |
| 5 and 6 | Tuning, and the first monthly report |

- [ ] Quality gate before go-live: run ten of the client's past BOQs. Go live only when every total matches theirs, or every difference is explained in writing
- [ ] Keep each client's files in their own storage folder, delete them on request, and never use client data in a demo
- [ ] Write a one-page runbook, "If it stops working", with five restart steps, and give it to one person you trust for weeks when you travel for work

## 9. Away-from-keyboard workflows

Eleven workflows answer, qualify, book, bill and publish while you are at Vesconite, and the only thing left for your evenings is the conversations themselves.

| # | Workflow | Starts when | What happens with no one there | Tool |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Front door | Someone submits any form on the site | Lead logged, reply S7 sent inside a minute with the demo video, four questions and the booking link, alert to your phone | Aurion Desk |
| 2 | WhatsApp | Someone messages the business number | Greeting, then an away message on weekdays 07:00 to 18:00 saying you reply after 18:00, with quick replies for audit, prices and the Checker | WhatsApp Business app |
| 3 | Booking | Someone picks an audit slot | Payment link, calendar invite, reminders at 24 hours and 1 hour, stage updated | Cal.com and Paystack or Yoco |
| 4 | Nurture | Someone ticks consent on the Checker or a form | Emails N1 to N5 on days 0, 2, 5, 9 and 14. Stops when they book | Brevo |
| 5 | Publishing | The scheduled time arrives | Reels on Tuesdays and posts on Thursdays, through 25 Mar | LinkedIn scheduler, Meta Business Suite, YouTube Studio |
| 6 | Evening queue | 17:30 on Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday | Ten next actions listed with drafted messages. You approve and send in 15 minutes | Aurion Desk |
| 7 | Daily digest | 18:00 every day | One message: new leads, replies, bookings, tickets, payments | Aurion Desk to Telegram |
| 8 | Support | A client emails support@ or a monitor fails | Ticket and acknowledgement S5, or an alert to your phone | Aurion Desk, UptimeRobot |
| 9 | Billing | The 1st of the month | Recurring invoices, debits, overdue reminders, and each client's monthly report | Zoho Invoice, Paystack or Yoco, Command Centre |
| 10 | Retention | Day 30 after go-live, each quarter, 60 days before a term ends | Testimonial ask R3, review-call reminder, renewal reminder | Aurion Desk |
| 11 | Newsletter | Last Saturday of the month | Draft built from that month's posts. You approve it | Aurion Desk and Brevo |

**Three things the machine never does:** quote a custom price, promise a delivery date, or say you are available during working hours.

## 11. From 4 Jan: the rhythm that keeps it running

After 4 Jan the business runs on eight hours a week in four fixed slots, and the workflows in section 9 cover everything between them.

| Slot | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| Tuesday 19:30 to 21:00 | Evening queue for 15 minutes, then an audit call or follow-ups. 10 LinkedIn invitations |
| Thursday 19:30 to 21:00 | Audit call, or plans and proposals. 10 LinkedIn invitations |
| Saturday 08:00 to 12:00 | Client delivery and onboarding, one new reel, 10 LinkedIn invitations |
| Sunday 17:00 to 18:00 | Scorecard, check next week's scheduled posts, reply to anything the machine flagged |

Read the 18:00 digest after work and nothing during it. Outreach to firms restarts on Tuesday 12 Jan, when the industry is back.

**Monthly:** the first Saturday is content day for next month's four reels and four posts. The last Saturday is the newsletter. The 1st bills itself.

**Scorecard, filled in every Sunday**

| Number | Weekly target |
| --- | --- |
| Live conversations of 20 minutes or more | 2 |
| Audits booked | 1 |
| Proposals sent | 1 a fortnight |
| LinkedIn invitations sent | 30 |
| Checker reports generated | 5 |
| Hours worked on Aurion | 8, never more than 10 |
| Recurring revenue | Recorded on the last Sunday of the month |

**When the third office signs,** hire a UP student for five hours a week at about R 150 an hour to build lists and render reels from your templates.
